qs.q: A child develops Lyme arthritis in the right knee months after a tick bite. Which histological feature is characteristic of the chronic synovitis seen in late Lyme arthritis?
o: Obliterative endarteritis with CD4+ T cells
Caseating granulomas with giant cell foci
qs.e: The histology of chronic Lyme arthritis characteristically shows synoviocyte hyperplasia, fibrin deposition, mononuclear cell infiltrates rich in CD4+ T cells, and obliterative endarteritis. Needle-shaped crystals are a classic feature of gout, not Lyme arthritis.
qs.s: Infectious Arthritis: Bacterial, TB & Viral Joint Infections: MCQs

qs.q: During the evaluation of a patient with suspected Lyme arthritis, two-tier serologic testing is performed. Which test combination is recommended for diagnosis?
o: Joint aspiration followed by Gram stain
qs.e: Serologic detection of anti-Borrelia antibodies using a two-tier approach of ELISA confirmed by Western blot is the recommended diagnostic method for Lyme arthritis. Ziehl-Neelsen staining is used for mycobacterial infections like tuberculosis.
